posts.body:
Yeah, I have the six tilesets, I think
But I can barely make anything with it. Or maybe I'm just not ingenuitive enough to create something out of nothing.
I'm also more familiar with RPGMaker XP's way of handling graphics, if that means anything.
I noticed in the first slot (A), there are graphics that change based on where you place them. This is a deviation from XP, where you had to insert them individually and make different spritesets for each tile.
I also noticed that the base resources don't have shop tiles, like tall counters, only long counters. In addition, the base tiles sometimes don't line up correctly, so you are limited on where you can place them.
For example, the kitchen tilesets must be placed near a corner and by an oven to complete the tileset "look" and not make it look broken off. This is really irritating because this will make it seem repetitive and reused assets.
I haven't seen anyone else's indoor tilesets, but I will post mine once I get the first village finished on this thread. Mind, it will mostly look the same for each different building.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
The autotile-heavy mapping system is one of the reasons I still use XP after all this time. I agree with you about the one-tile-high tables not looking as nice as the XP ones that are similar proportions, but arranged over 2 tiles instead. I agree that it makes the counters look a bit weird and out of place.
But you don't
have
to use the autotile counters. You have four other pages of tile sheets--the ones labeled B through E--that you can use just like XP. A full tileset in MV/Z (one that uses all of the B-E pages) holds the same amount of tiles as a  XP tileset about 7000px long, I don't recall the exact number off the top of my head. XP had more individual tilesets, but none of them were anywhere near that big.
Avery has a bunch of tutorials on small tweaks to make the RTP furniture fit more naturally on a map, among many other absolutely phenomenal tutorials on everything from making tiles to making maps. Those little tweaks go a long way toward making the default resources look nicer!
There are also entire sections of the forum dedicated to free resources made by very skilled and very generous forum members, all of which have extremely reasonable terms of use. Google is your friend, yes; but Resource Central an even better friend. Browse the threads, or use the forum search function. There's a lot of treasure to be found here.

posts.author: pawsplay
posts.body:
If I have a map where I want counters and such to sit a bit up, I just create an extra tile sheet and put the edited tiles on it. You can literally just slide them a few pixels up, and just decide for yourself whether the upper or lower half should be walkable, depending on the object.
You can create "long counters" by using the auto-table tiles.
